extracted.intended_audience: general readers and travelers (readers of travel humor/pilgrimage accounts)
extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt of a humorous 19th-century travelogue (Mark Twain) offering observational advice and complaints about pilgrimage, sightseeing, guides, and travel practices; useful as informal guidelines for travelers and as examples of travel-writing satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time to appreciate sights
rubrics_metrics.description: One can not see such things at an instant glance -- one frequently only finds out how really beautiful a really beautiful woman is after considerable acquaintance with her; and the rule applies to Niagara Falls, to majestic mountains and to mosques -- especially to mosques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not expect to grasp the full beauty or significance of major monuments and natural wonders from a cursory glance; plan for extended, deliberate acquaintance rather than snap judgments. Examples: spend more time with large sites (mosques, falls, mountains) to appreciate them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't compress too many sights into one day
rubrics_metrics.description: Our pilgrims compress too much into one day. One can gorge sights to repletion as well as sweetmeats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overloading itineraries; crowding many attractions into a single day leads to fatigue and diminished appreciation. Leave time to look deliberately and to reflect on what you've seen so it becomes a lasting memory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take unescorted walks to escape guide volubility
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a very relief to steal a walk of a hundred yards without a guide along to talk unceasingly about every stone you step upon and drag you back ages and ages to the day when it achieved celebrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule breaks from guided tours; solitary or small-group wandering can provide respite from continual commentary and allow personal observation and contemplation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce diversions to prevent group demoralization
rubrics_metrics.description: This disposition to smoke, and idle and talk, was not well. It was plain that it must not be allowed to gain ground. A diversion must be tried, or demoralization would ensue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a traveling party becomes listless from fatigue or routine, plan a change (different destination, ride, or activity) to restore energy and interest; monitor group morale and act before apathy spreads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be skeptical of guide lore and invented traditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide was perfectly serene. He said, calmly, 'This is one of the stones that would have cried out.' It was of little use to try to shake this fellow's simple faith--it was easy to see that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides may repeat local legends or make claims without evidence; travelers should treat such stories skeptically and seek corroboration rather than accepting every asserted 'authentic' relic or tradition at face value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch for staged dangers and mutual-profit scams
rubrics_metrics.description: The Bedouins that attacked the other parties of pilgrims so fiercely were provided for the occasion by the Arab guards of those parties, and shipped from Jerusalem for temporary service as Bedouins...The nuisance of an Arab guard is one which is created by the Sheiks and the Bedouins together, for mutual profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to the possibility that reported threats, guards, or escorts may be contrived for extortion or theatrical effect; verify risks and the necessity of paid guards rather than assuming all dangers are real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious when giving money to beggars and intermediaries
rubrics_metrics.description: The guide wanted us to give them some money, and we did it; but when he went on to say that they were starving to death we could not but feel that we had done a great sin...and so we tried to collect it back, but it could not be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise discretion when giving alms; demands may be inflated by intermediaries. Consider local context and the potential for pressure or exploitation before handing over money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept that repetitive sightseeing diminishes fascination
rubrics_metrics.description: We are surfeited with sights. Nothing has any fascination for us, now, but the Church of the Holy Sepulchre. We have been there every day, and have not grown tired of it; but we are weary of every thing else.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that too much exposure to similar or numerous attractions can blunt interest; prioritize a few meaningful places rather than attempting to see everything superficially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand memory formation — distance/time improve perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: When one is in Rome, all the domes are alike; but when he has gone away twelve miles, the city fades utterly from sight and leaves St. Peter's swelling above the level plain like an anchored balloon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realize that perspective on travel experiences often improves with time and distance; some impressions become clearer and more meaningful after leaving the immediate scene, so preserve recollections rather than forcing instant judgments.
